name: Pagely
tagline: Premium managed WordPress hosting on AWS for high-traffic, enterprise sites
description: Pagely is a premium managed WordPress hosting provider built on Amazon Web Services, aimed at enterprise and high-traffic sites rather than budget shoppers — plans run through its proprietary Atomic control panel with no cPanel option.
about: Pagely's plans run in two tiers: Performance (StartPress $99/mo, DevPress $199/mo, LitePress $299/mo) and Pro (ProPress $499/mo, PowerPress $999/mo), with a custom-priced Enterprise tier (ScalePress) for large-scale deployments. Site allowances scale from 5 sites on StartPress up to 60 on PowerPress, storage runs 30-50GB SSD depending on tier, and none of the plans cap visitors or pageviews — bandwidth and CDN allowances scale by tier instead. All plans run on AWS infrastructure through Pagely's own Atomic control panel rather than cPanel, and include PressCACHE, a global WordPress CDN and free site migrations.

This is not a budget host: the entry-level StartPress plan runs $99/month (list price $199, with promotional pricing sometimes bringing it down), several multiples of what mainstream shared hosts charge. Some features are tier-gated rather than universal — PressTHUMB image optimization and WordPress Multisite support are absent on LitePress and below, and Elasticsearch is only available on Pro-tier plans and above, so check the specific plan's feature list before assuming a lower tier covers everything a larger site needs.
policies: Pagely does not publish a standard money-back guarantee window on its pricing page — confirm current refund terms directly with Pagely sales before purchasing, since this varies from the 30-day guarantees common at budget hosts.

faqs.a: No — Pagely runs its own proprietary control panel called Atomic instead of cPanel. It's built specifically for managing WordPress sites on Pagely's AWS infrastructure rather than general-purpose hosting management.

faqs.q: Does Pagely cap visitors or pageviews?
faqs.a: No — Pagely doesn't cap visitors or pageviews on any plan. Instead, plans are differentiated by number of sites allowed, storage, bandwidth and CDN allowance, which is a different model from hosts that throttle traffic past a visitor limit.

faqs.q: How much does Pagely cost to start?
faqs.a: Pagely's entry-level Performance-tier plan, StartPress, starts at $99/month (list price $199/month) for up to 5 WordPress sites, 30GB SSD storage and 50GB bandwidth. Pricing scales up through DevPress ($199/mo) and LitePress ($299/mo) before reaching the Pro tier at $499+/month.

faqs.q: Is Pagely a good fit for small, low-budget sites?
faqs.a: Generally no — Pagely is positioned for enterprise and high-traffic sites, with pricing several times higher than mainstream shared hosts. Small sites with modest budgets are typically better served by a budget host and should only consider Pagely if they specifically need AWS-backed managed WordPress infrastructure at scale.
